turns.text: She said she felt like I’d been distant for months. Maybe she’s right. But I didn’t know it was that bad. I keep thinking if I’d noticed, maybe this wouldn’t have happened.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It’s hard to hold both things at once: maybe she felt distant from you, and her choice to sleep with her ex was still hers. You didn’t know how serious it felt to her. Would it help to talk through what you want to do next, or would you rather stay with how this feels right now?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I don’t know. I still love her, which makes me feel stupid. I guess I want to know if there’s any way back from this, but I can’t even look at her right now.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: Loving her doesn’t make you stupid. You can love her and still feel deeply hurt, and you don’t have to decide whether there’s a way back while everything is so raw. What feels most unbearable about seeing her right now?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I’m scared I’ll either yell at her or just break down. And if she apologizes, I’m scared I’ll forgive her before I’ve even figured out what I want.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds like you’re trying to protect yourself from being swept into a decision before you’re ready. You’re allowed to take some space and tell her you can’t talk about what happens next yet. Is there someone you trust you could be with or talk to tonight?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My sister, probably. I haven’t told her yet. Maybe I’ll call her and just say I don’t want to be alone with this tonight.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds like a gentle, clear way to ask for what you need tonight. You don’t have to explain everything at once. I’m glad you’ve thought of your sister—what do you think might make it easier to call her?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I don’t even know where to start. He cheated on me, then left me to deal with all of it alone. I feel completely crushed.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds devastating—being betrayed and then left alone with the hurt. I’m glad you told me. What feels heaviest right now?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I keep thinking about how long he’d stopped trying. I was making excuses for him, waiting for things to get better. I wish I’d left sooner.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It sounds like you’re looking back with a lot of regret, while also grieving how long you kept hoping things would change. You were trying to make sense of someone you loved, not failing a test. What are you blaming yourself for most right now?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That I stayed. I saw the signs, but I kept thinking if I was more patient, or easier to love, he’d care again. I feel stupid for believing that.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: You weren’t stupid for hoping someone you loved would meet you with care. It sounds like you’re turning his choices into a verdict on your worth, and that’s a painful burden to carry. What would you say to someone you love if they blamed themselves for staying?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I’d tell them it wasn’t their fault he cheated. But I can’t make myself believe that about me. I just feel so empty.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That emptiness sounds frightening, especially when the kindness you’d offer someone else feels out of reach for you. You don’t have to force yourself to believe it all at once. Are you thinking of ending your life? You can call or text 988, the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline, at any time.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: No, I’m not thinking of ending my life. I just don’t know how to get through the day without feeling like this. I can barely make myself do anything.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: I’m glad you’re safe, and I’m sorry the hurt is making even ordinary things feel so hard. When you say you can barely do anything, it sounds like this is weighing on your whole day. turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I haven’t eaten much today. Maybe I should try to have something, but even deciding what feels like too much.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: When you’re this drained, even choosing food can feel like another task. Would it help to make it very simple—something already within reach, even a snack or a few bites?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I just feel awful about how I look lately. I don’t even want people to see me.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It sounds painful to feel so uncomfortable being seen. I’m glad you told me. Are you thinking about hiding away, or are you also thinking about hurting yourself?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I’m not thinking about hurting myself. I just want to avoid everyone. I’ve been feeling really bad about my body.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds exhausting, especially when it makes being around people feel hard. Would it help more to talk about what’s been making you feel bad about your body, or about how to get through seeing people right now?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I’ve gained about 30 pounds over the last two years. I hate how I look now. I’ve been avoiding food and waiting until I’m almost passing out before I eat. Yesterday I didn’t eat until 7 pm.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds frightening and lonely, and waiting until you’re nearly passing out can put your safety at risk. I’m glad you told me. turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I could text my sister, I think. Eating feels really hard, though. I’m scared I’ll feel worse about myself afterward.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It makes sense that eating feels tied to the fear and shame about your body. Texting your sister could help you not be alone with this. Would you like help finding a simple way to tell her what’s going on?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yeah. I don’t know how to say it without making it sound dramatic.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It doesn’t have to sound dramatic to be worth taking seriously. You could text: “Hey, I’ve been struggling with eating and how I feel about my body. turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Maybe. I could send that. I still feel ashamed, though.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: Feeling ashamed doesn’t mean you’ve done anything wrong; you’re dealing with something hard, and reaching out is a caring step. Could you send it as written, or would a shorter text feel easier?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I don’t even know where to start. Work just stopped, and I have no idea when I’ll get paid again. I’m trying not to panic, but it’s a lot.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds really unsettling—your income stopping without knowing when it’ll return can make everything feel uncertain. I’m glad you said it. Would it help to talk through what feels most urgent right now, or would you rather I just stay with you for a moment?

turns.speaker: user

turns.text: Not knowing the timeline makes it hard to plan, and I can hear how exhausting those circles feel. Would it help to make a simple picture of what money you have, what’s coming in, and the essential bills due soon?

turns.speaker: user

turns.text: That makes sense; looking at the numbers could feel like facing the fear head-on, especially with rent coming up. We can go gently and focus just on what’s due before your next expected income, without trying to solve everything at once. Would that feel manageable?

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It sounds like you’re trying to balance covering rent now with keeping a little security for later. I can’t know what amount is right without the full picture, but we can lay out the essentials and the savings you have, then see what choices feel possible. What’s the rent amount?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: It’s $1,600. I’ve got around $3,000 in savings, and then groceries and utilities on top of that. It doesn’t feel like much of a cushion.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That does sound like a thin cushion, especially with your income uncertain. We can map out the next month without deciding anything yet: about how much are groceries and utilities for a month?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Groceries are maybe $400, utilities around $200. Then there’s my car payment too, $350. Just saying it all out loud is making my chest tight.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That’s a lot to hold at once, and I’m sorry it’s tightening your chest. We can pause the numbers for a moment. Would it help to take one slow breath with me, or would you rather keep talking through the money?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I keep feeling like I could do better in school. I tell myself if I could just write better, my grades would be better too.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It sounds like you’re putting a lot of pressure on your writing, as if it’s the one thing holding your grades back. What feels hardest about writing for school?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I think I know what I want to say, but when I actually write it, it comes out messy. Then I get stuck worrying it sounds stupid.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds frustrating—you have ideas, but worrying how they’ll sound makes it harder to get them onto the page. Would it help to talk through a simple way to get a rough draft down without judging it yet?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Maybe. I just feel like I should already be able to do this, though. Other people make it look easy.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It can feel discouraging when everyone else seems to manage it effortlessly, but writing often looks easier from the outside than it feels. Would it help to try one small way of getting your ideas down, or would you rather stay with how this is feeling for a moment?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I guess we can try something small. I just don’t want it to turn into another thing I’m doing wrong.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That makes sense—you don’t need another standard to measure yourself against. We can treat this as an experiment, not a test: write one idea as a messy sentence, then add “because…” and say why you think it. What’s one idea from an assignment you’re working on?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I have an essay about a book. I know the main character is lonely, but I don’t know how to make that sound like an actual point.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: You already have the start of a point: you’re noticing something important about the character. We can keep it simple for now: “The main character’s loneliness matters because…” What do you think their loneliness changes or helps the reader understand?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Maybe it makes them act distant, even when they want someone to understand them. I don’t know if that’s enough to say.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That’s enough for a starting idea, and it has a real tension in it: they want connection but act distant. You could write, “The character’s loneliness makes them seem distant, even though they want to be understood.” What moment in the book makes you think of that?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I don’t know. I just feel like I’m wasting my life at this job. It’s hard to admit that.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds painful to admit, like part of you is worried your time is slipping by. What feels most missing from your life right now?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I guess I want to feel like what I do matters. Most days I just get through the work and go home, and then I feel ashamed for not being more grateful.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It sounds like you’re craving a sense of purpose, and then judging yourself for feeling that way. Wanting your work to matter doesn’t mean you’re ungrateful. Would it help to talk about what “mattering” would look like for you?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Maybe doing something that helps people, or making something I can actually point to and say, I did that. Right now everything feels so abstract. But I don’t even know if I’m capable of doing anything different.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: You’re longing for something tangible and useful, and the uncertainty about your abilities makes that feel far away. What’s one thing you’ve done, at work or outside it, that left you feeling even a little proud or useful?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I used to volunteer at a food pantry on weekends. I liked that you could see people leave with what they needed. I stopped when work got busy, and I feel bad about that too.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds like a clear kind of meaning for you: seeing something you did help someone right away. And stopping when work got busy doesn’t erase what you gave. Would you like to think together about whether there’s a manageable way to reconnect with that, or would you rather stay with how you’re feeling?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I think maybe a manageable way. I’m not sure I can go back every weekend, but maybe once a month wouldn’t feel impossible. I still feel guilty that I let it drop.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It sounds like once a month feels possible, while the guilt is still hanging around. You could treat one visit as a small experiment, not a promise to make up for the past. Would it help to send the pantry a quick message and ask what monthly shifts they have?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Maybe. I could send a message. I think I was making it all-or-nothing in my head—like if I can’t be really committed, there’s no point. Once a month feels less overwhelming.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That all-or-nothing pressure sounds heavy; it’s a relief to find a smaller step that still matters. What would make sending the message feel easy enough today?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I guess… my friends keep calling me a weirdo because I don’t talk much. It gets to me more than I let on.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It sounds like their teasing is landing on a tender spot, even if you hide how much it hurts. You’re not wrong for being quiet. What do you wish your friends understood about you?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I wish they’d understand I’m not ignoring them or trying to be rude. I just don’t always know what to say… and then they get annoyed, so I end up keeping to myself even more.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds like a painful loop: feeling unsure what to say, then their annoyance making it even harder to join in. Would it help to think of a simple way to explain that to them, or would you rather stay with how it feels right now?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I’d rather stay with how it feels for a bit. I feel like I’m always the one who has to explain myself. It’s tiring.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It sounds exhausting to feel misunderstood and then have to do the work of making everyone else understand. You deserve room to be quiet without being treated as rude. I’m here with you. What part of that feels heaviest right now?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Mostly feeling like I don’t really belong with them. Even when I’m there, I feel kind of outside the group.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: Feeling outside the group while you’re right there with them can be especially lonely. I’m glad you told me. Has this been happening with these friends for a while?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yeah, for a while now. It’s not every single time, but enough that I start wondering if they even want me there.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That uncertainty can wear on you, especially when it happens often enough to make you question your place. What do they do that leaves you wondering whether they want you there?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Usually they make plans while I’m there and don’t really include me, or they joke that I’m weird when I don’t say much. I can’t tell if they mean it seriously or not.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That would leave a lot of people feeling left out, even if the jokes are meant playfully. It makes sense you’re unsure how to read it. When they make plans in front of you, do they ever invite you along?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I’m just so tired of this. Every time it feels like things might change, quarantine gets extended again. I can’t see an end to it.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It sounds exhausting to keep hoping for an end, only to have it pushed further away. I’m glad you told me. Are you thinking of ending your life? You can call or text 988, the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline, at any time.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: No. I’m not thinking of ending my life. I just feel stuck and angry, and lately it’s hard to care about much.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: I’m glad you’re not thinking of ending your life. Feeling stuck and angry, with little to care about, sounds really draining. Has this been getting in the way of sleep or everyday things lately?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yeah. My sleep is all over the place, and I’ve been putting off basic stuff. Some days I barely get dressed. I don’t really know how to make myself care.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds like a heavy slump, and even basic things taking effort can make the days feel smaller. Would it help to think together about one small, manageable thing for today?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Maybe. I could try to shower, but even that feels like a whole project right now.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: When even a shower feels huge, it makes sense to break it down rather than force the whole thing. Would it feel doable to just turn on the water, or would a smaller step—like washing your face—feel better today?

turns.text: I don’t know. I’m tired of turning everything into a task list. It’s not really the shower. I just miss having a life that feels like mine.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: You’re right—I turned what you said into another task, when you’re grieving how much of your life feels out of your hands. I’m sorry. What do you miss most about feeling like your life is yours?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I miss seeing my friends without planning it like some complicated event. And just being able to go somewhere without wondering if it’s safe. I feel like I’m watching my life instead of living it.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds lonely and unsettling—like the ordinary freedom to be with people has been replaced by constant calculation. I won’t rush to turn that into a plan. What’s it like for you when you notice that feeling most strongly?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I’m really scared I’m going to lose my job after Christmas. I keep trying not to think about it, but I can’t.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That uncertainty sounds frightening, and trying to push it away may be making it harder to get a little relief. What feels most worrying about losing your job?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Mostly that I won’t know what to do next. It’s a small company, and they were counting on this new stimulus funding. If it doesn’t come through, I don’t know how long they can keep us on.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It sounds like the funding is out of your hands, and the unknown is making it hard to picture a next step. Would it help to think through a few options together, or would you rather stay with how scary this feels for a bit?

turns.speaker: user

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds like a tight spot: the bills are real, and there isn’t much cushion, so it makes sense that your mind keeps circling. We can keep this very small—would it help to start by figuring out what bills are due before Christmas?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Maybe. Rent is due at the start of the month, and then my car payment. I’m not even sure when I’ll hear from work about the funding. They keep saying they’re waiting.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: Waiting without a clear timeline leaves you carrying the uncertainty on your own. We could start with one small step: would it feel manageable to ask your manager when they expect to know, and whether they can give you a heads-up before any job changes?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I could ask, I guess. I just don’t want to sound like I’m panicking or make them think I’m already looking to leave. But not knowing is eating at me.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: You’re trying to get clarity without making it seem like you’ve given up on the job. turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That sounds less intense than what I had in my head. I could probably send something like that. I still feel pretty anxious, though. I keep thinking about what happens if they say there’s no money.

turns.speaker: helper
